answer: Every content project starts as a garden. You plant seeds in public, water them daily, and most weeks nothing sprouts. A jade plant is honest that way: it grows slowly, survives neglect, and never pretends to be a tree. My trellis is a simple routine — one post, one honest metric, one lesson written down before midnight. Some weeks the vines go sideways, and that is fine. Building in public means the trellis shows the gaps too. People do not stay because the garden is perfect; they stay because the gardener keeps showing up even when nothing blooms. Slow growth is still growth.
